answer: Each agent registers a temporary violet token generated from a cryptographic hash of a unique hardware‑derived nonce and a network‑wide signal timestamp. In the commit‑reveal phase the agent first posts the hash, then at the zenith of the round reveals the nonce; peers verify the hash matches, forcing any Sybil to produce a fresh token for every identity. Because the nonce cannot be precomputed, the attacker must expend fresh computational work and hardware entropy for each fake node, making large‑scale impersonation prohibitively costly.
